title: How the Zscaler Terraform providers store, log, and send secrets

c2c-ir-secrets-not-sensitive.statement: The ZIA `zia_dlp_cloud_to_cloud_ir` data source declares the nested `tenant_authorization_info` attributes `client_secret`, `user_pwd`, `secret_token` and others as plain Computed strings. The schema does not set `Sensitive` on them.

quotes: "client_secret": { Type: schema.TypeString, Computed: true, Description: "Client secret for authorization",
"secret_token": { Type: schema.TypeString, Computed: true, Description: "Secret token for authorization",
"user_pwd": { Type: schema.TypeString, Computed: true, Description: "User password for authorization",

upstream.note: Filing 9 (credential handling) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

c2c-ir-secrets-copied-to-state.statement: The same data source's flattener copies the secret-bearing members of the API response (`client_secret`, `secret_token`, `user_pwd`, `org_api_key`, `cred_json`, `credentials`, `access_token`, `bot_token`) into those attributes, so whatever the API returns for them is written into the data source's state.
c2c-ir-secrets-copied-to-state.conditions: State receives these values only if the API actually returns them populated on read (gap api-returns-secrets).

upstream.note: Filing 9 (credential handling) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

c2c-ir-entity-log-includes-secrets.statement: The same data source logs `resp.OnboardableEntity` with `%+v`. That value is a pointer to a struct that holds `TenantAuthorizationInfo` by value, so the formatted line prints the secret-bearing members' contents (verified by running the same shape through `fmt` with `%+v`). The line is prefixed `[DEBUG]` and has no redaction.
c2c-ir-entity-log-includes-secrets.conditions: Appears in output only when the provider's debug-level log output is enabled (the line carries a `[DEBUG]` text prefix; how that maps to a visible level is not shown here) and when the API returned the values (gap api-returns-secrets).

upstream.note: Filing 9 (credential handling) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

c2c-ir-response-log-prints-pointer-only.statement: The line above it, `Retrieved cloud-to-cloud IR: %+v` on the whole response, does not print the secrets: the response holds `OnboardableEntity` as a pointer, which `%+v` renders as an address, not its contents. One of the audit's leads said this line leaks the credentials; the code shows only the entity line does.

cloud-nss-and-admin-token-in-state.statement: Two more ZIA data sources export credentials as plain Computed strings and write them to state: `zia_cloud_nss_server` (`authentication_token`, `client_secret`) and `zia_admin_users` (the `token` inside `exec_mobile_app_tokens`).

quotes: "authentication_token": { Type: schema.TypeString, Computed: true, Description: "The authentication token value",
"client_secret": { Type: schema.TypeString, Computed: true, Description: "Client secret applicable when SIEM type is set to S3 or Azure Sentinel",

cloud-nss-and-admin-token-in-state.conditions: State receives these only if the API returns the values on read (gap api-returns-secrets).

upstream.note: Filing 9 (credential handling) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

zia-data-source-secret-attributes-unmark.statement: No ZIA data source schema marks any of the secret-named attributes above `Sensitive`. Searching the ZIA data sources for attribute names containing secret, password, pwd, passphrase, token, api_key, psk, private_key, cred_json or credentials finds these unmarked instances: the Cloud-to-Cloud IR authorization attributes, `zia_cloud_nss_server` `authentication_token` and `client_secret`, and `zia_admin_users` `token`. The matches that are not secrets (such as `is_password_login_allowed`) are ignored. A name search also misses values that can carry secrets under other names, such as the cloud NSS server's `connection_headers`.
zia-data-source-secret-attributes-unmark.conditions: Absence claim from a search at tf-zia v4.8.3: `git grep -n -i -E '"[a-z_]*(secret|password|pwd|passphrase|token|api_key|psk|private_key|cred_json|credentials)[a-z_]*": *\{' v4.8.3 -- 'zia/data_source_*.go'`, with `git grep -n 'Sensitive: *true'` returning, among data sources, only `pre_shared_key` in `data_source_zia_location_management.go`. Attribute-name matching misses secrets with other names, and the search covers v4.8.3 only. The list names every unmarked secret attribute found, not every secret the API can return.

upstream.note: Filing 9 (credential handling) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

zia-psk-handled-differently.statement: The ZIA data sources are not uniform. In `zia_location_management` the nested `pre_shared_key` is marked `Sensitive: true`. In `zia_traffic_forwarding_vpn_credentials` the `Sensitive: true` line is commented out, and so is the line that would set `pre_shared_key` from the response, so that data source declares the attribute but does not populate it.

quotes: "pre_shared_key": { Type: schema.TypeString, Computed: true, Sensitive: true, },

pra-create-sanitizer-mutates-request.statement: `zpa_pra_credential_controller` create expands the configured secrets into the request struct, then calls `sanitizeFields(&req)` before sending it. `sanitizeFields` writes the literal `***REDACTED***` into the request's string fields whose lowercased name contains `password` or `passphrase`. The mutated struct is what is passed to `pracredential.Create`, so the create request carries the sentinel in `password` and `passphrase` instead of the configured values (including when those fields were left empty in the configuration).
pra-create-sanitizer-mutates-request.conditions: What the ZPA API stores when it receives the sentinel (reject, or accept as the secret) is server behavior (gap api-pra-sentinel).

upstream.note: Filing 9 (credential handling) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

sanitizer-misses-private-key.statement: The sanitizer compares the lowercased Go field name with `private_key`, but the struct field is `PrivateKey`, which lowercases to `privatekey` and does not contain `private_key`. So on create the SSH private key is not replaced: it is sent as configured, while `password` and `passphrase` are replaced. Running the same matching logic over a struct with these field names redacts `Password` and `Passphrase` and leaves `PrivateKey` unchanged. The audit lead said all three secrets are replaced; the code shows two.

upstream.note: Filing 9 (credential handling) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

pra-create-log-prints-private-key.statement: The create path logs the request after sanitizing it, with `%+v`. Because the sanitizer leaves `PrivateKey` unchanged, that INFO log line contains the SSH private key in clear text when one is configured, while `password` and `passphrase` show the sentinel. The line is logged on every create, at INFO level.

quotes: log.Printf("[INFO] Creating credential controller with request\n%+v\n", req)

pra-create-log-prints-private-key.conditions: Depends on the provider's log output being enabled for that line (the INFO-prefixed line is written by the standard logger; how Terraform surfaces it is not shown here), and on the private key being set.

upstream.note: Filing 9 (credential handling) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

pra-update-omits-empty-secrets.statement: On update the provider expands the secrets with `d.Get` and sends the PUT without sanitizing, so a changed secret is sent as configured. A secret that is empty in config becomes an empty Go string, and the SDK struct tags are `omitempty`, so the field is left out of the PUT body. An update cannot send an explicit empty value to clear a stored `password`, `passphrase` or `private_key`.
pra-update-omits-empty-secrets.conditions: Whether the API clears a stored secret when the field is absent from a PUT, or keeps it, is server behavior (gap api-pra-empty-secret).

upstream.note: Filing 9 (credential handling) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

pra-read-never-sets-secrets.statement: The resource's read sets `name`, `description`, `credential_type`, `username` and `microtenant_id` and nothing else. The three secret attributes are `Sensitive: true` in the schema but are never refreshed from the API, so their state is whatever the configuration supplied. After a create that sent the sentinel, the next plan shows no difference for the secrets. Read does log the whole API response at INFO with `%+v`, which would print any secret the API returns (gap api-returns-secrets).

quotes: "password": { Type: schema.TypeString, Optional: true, Sensitive: true,

pra-read-never-sets-secrets.conditions: Absence search at tf-zpa v4.4.10 and HEAD: `git grep -n 'Set("password"\|Set("passphrase"\|Set("private_key"' <ref> -- zpa/resource_zpa_pra_credential_controller.go` returns nothing. That unset attributes keep their prior state value is Terraform plugin SDK behavior, not shown in this repository.

upstream.note: Filing 9 (credential handling) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

pra-data-source-password-declared-not-se.statement: The `zpa_pra_credential_controller` data source declares `password` as a Computed string without `Sensitive`, but its read never sets it, so the attribute is always empty. This is a missing output, and as written it keeps the password out of state. If it were set without also adding `Sensitive: true`, it would be a plain-text state value like the ZIA cases.

quotes: "password": { Type: schema.TypeString, Computed: true, Description: "The password associated with the username for the login you want to use for the privileged credential",

pra-data-source-password-declared-not-se.conditions: Absence search at tf-zpa v4.4.10 and HEAD: `git grep -n 'Set("password"' <ref> -- zpa/data_source_zpa_pra_credential_controller.go` returns nothing. The last sentence is a consequence of changing the code, not something the code does now.

upstream.note: Filing 9 (credential handling) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

sanitizer-call-sites.statement: `sanitizeFields` is called in two places in the ZPA provider: PRA credential create and PRA credential pool create. The update path of the PRA credential does not call it. In the pool, the request struct has no field whose name contains `password`, `passphrase` or `private_key`, so the call changes nothing there.
sanitizer-call-sites.conditions: Search at tf-zpa v4.4.10 and HEAD: `git grep -n sanitizeFields <ref> -- zpa` returns the definition in zpa/utils.go, `zpa/resource_zpa_pra_credential_controller.go:126` and `zpa/resource_zpa_pra_credential_pool.go:109`.

upstream.note: Filing 9 (credential handling) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

sdk-logs-full-bodies-when-enabled.statement: When `ZSCALER_SDK_LOG` and `ZSCALER_SDK_VERBOSE` are both true, the SDK dumps every request including its body, and every response, in full, with no redaction of secret fields or of the Authorization header. The ZIA and ZPA providers set both through `WithDebug` whenever `TF_LOG` is DEBUG or TRACE, so ordinary provider debug logging is enough on the OneAPI path. Provider-side redaction does not affect these dumps: they show what is on the wire, such as the sentinel in `password` and `passphrase` and the unredacted `privateKey` on a PRA create, or a returned credential on a read.

quotes: // Enable SDK debug logging when Terraform debug logging is enabled
// Enable SDK debug logging when Terraform debug logging is enabled

sdk-logs-full-bodies-when-enabled.conditions: The dump lines are `[DEBUG]`-prefixed and the default logger drops them unless `ZSCALER_SDK_VERBOSE` is true; `WithDebug` sets both variables. The legacy ZPA client path does not call `WithDebug`, so there both variables must be set by hand. Response bodies contain secrets only if the API returns them (gap api-returns-secrets).

api-returns-secrets.title: Whether the ZIA read APIs return secret values in clear
api-returns-secrets.blocks: saying that Cloud-to-Cloud IR, Cloud NSS and admin-user secrets actually reach state or logs, rather than only being exposed if returned
api-returns-secrets.detail: The provider copies whatever the SDK struct decodes. The sources do not say whether the ZIA API masks, omits or returns these fields on GET. Test in a scratch tenant: create a Cloud-to-Cloud IR, a Cloud NSS server with an authentication token and an admin with an Executive Insights token, read each through its API, and note whether the secret members are present in clear, masked or absent.

api-pra-sentinel.title: What the ZPA API does with the literal ***REDACTED*** in a PRA credential create
api-pra-sentinel.blocks: saying whether a PRA credential created through the provider is unusable, rejected, or stored with the sentinel as its secret
api-pra-sentinel.detail: The provider sends the sentinel in `password` and `passphrase`. Nothing captured says whether ZPA validates, rejects or stores it. Test in a scratch tenant by creating a credential with the provider and then checking whether a console session using it authenticates.

api-pra-empty-secret.title: What the ZPA API does when a PRA credential PUT omits a secret
api-pra-empty-secret.blocks: saying whether removing a secret from configuration clears it in ZPA or silently keeps the old value
api-pra-empty-secret.detail: The provider omits empty secrets from the PUT body. Test in a scratch tenant by updating a credential with a password to one without and reading it back for a changed state, and by using the credential.
